record.original_question: Improve the known lower bounds in the Hilbert-XVI-type comparison table between polynomial systems and piecewise linear systems separated by an algebraic curve branch: H(2) >= 4 versus L(1) >= 3, H(3) >= 13 versus L(2) >= 4, and H(n) >= K n^2/log(n) versus L(n) >= floor(n/2).

evidence.quote: Problem 18. Improve, if possible, the lower bounds of this table: Polynomial case H(2) >= 4, H(3) >= 13, H(n) >= K n^2/log(n); Linear piecewise case L(1) >= 3, L(2) >= 4, L(n) >= [n/2].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For each integer n ≥ 1, define the following two Hilbert-type numbers.

(a) Polynomial Hilbert number H(n): the supremum, over all planar polynomial vector fields
    x' = P(x,y),   y' = Q(x,y)
with deg P, deg Q ≤ n, of the number of isolated periodic orbits (limit cycles) of the system.

(b) Piecewise linear number L(n): the supremum, over all planar discontinuous piecewise linear vector fields of the form
    (x',y') = A^+(x,y) + b^+   if  Φ(x,y) > 0,
    (x',y') = A^-(x,y) + b^-   if  Φ(x,y) < 0,
where A^± are 2×2 real matrices, b^± ∈ ℝ², and the discontinuity set {Φ = 0} is a single irreducible branch of a real algebraic curve of degree n, of the number of crossing limit cycles of the system.

The currently known unconditional lower bounds are
    H(2) ≥ 4,    H(3) ≥ 13,    H(n) ≥ K · n² / log n  for some absolute constant K > 0,
    L(1) ≥ 3,    L(2) ≥ 4,     L(n) ≥ ⌊n/2⌋.

Problem. Improve any of these six lower bounds: produce explicit families of polynomial (respectively, piecewise linear) systems exhibiting strictly more limit cycles than the bounds above guarantee, for the corresponding value(s) of n.
artifact.status_search_result: The polynomial bounds H(2) ≥ 4, H(3) ≥ 13, and H(n) ≥ K n²/log n remain the best known unconditional lower bounds in the literature. For the piecewise linear case with algebraic curve separation, recent work (e.g., on systems separated by y = x^n and related classes) has established improved lower bounds for L(n) for specific small n and specific separation curves, but a complete improvement of all six listed bounds has not been achieved. The general problem is still open.

status_evidence.title: The 16th Hilbert Problem for Discontinuous Piecewise Linear Differential Systems Separated by the Algebraic Curve y=x^n
status_evidence.snippet: Studies maximum number of crossing limit cycles for piecewise linear systems separated by y=x^n, providing lower bounds depending on n.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work provides lower bounds for L(n) for specific algebraic separation curves, partially advancing the piecewise linear side of the table.

status_evidence.title: On the Hilbert number for piecewise linear vector fields with algebraic discontinuity set
status_evidence.snippet: Investigates Hilbert number for piecewise linear vector fields with algebraic discontinuity set.
status_evidence.claim: Bounds for L(n) in the algebraic-discontinuity setting are an active research topic with partial improvements.

status_evidence.title: Hilbert's sixteenth problem - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: H(n) is unknown for n>1; standard known lower bound H(n) ≥ K n^2/log n.
status_evidence.claim: The general polynomial lower bound H(n) ≥ K n^2/log n remains the standard known bound.
